slot.brief: Give wavelength of electromagnetic radiation; ask energy of one photon and of one mole of photons in kJ.

stem: Radiation of wavelength $600$ nm is used. Find the energy of one photon and of one mole of photons. Take $h=6.626\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=3.00\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$ and $N_A=6.022\times10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: E = hc/λ = (6.626×10⁻³⁴)(3.00×10⁸)/(600×10⁻⁹) = 3.31×10⁻¹⁹ J per photon. Per mole: E N_A = 199.5 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{(6.626\times10^{-34})(3.00\times10^8)}{600\times10^{-9}}=3.31\times10^{-19}$ J
$E_{\mathrm{mol}}=EN_A=1.996\times10^5$ J mol$^{-1}=199.6$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

Independent check: E = hc/λ = (6.626×10⁻³⁴)(3.00×10⁸)/(600×10⁻⁹) = 3.31×10⁻¹⁹ J per photon. Per mole: E N_A = 199.5 kJ mol⁻¹.
solution:
The energy of one photon is $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.
$$E=\dfrac{(6.626\times10^{-34})(3.00\times10^8)}{600\times10^{-9}}=3.31\times10^{-19}\text{ J}$$
For one mole of photons, $E_{\mathrm{mol}}=EN_A=(3.31\times10^{-19})(6.022\times10^{23})=199.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

C: doubles the photon energy and hence the molar energy.
D: underestimates the photon energy and molar energy.
